Level surfaces of a trivariate function

Source: R/layers-stats-volumes.R
stat_isofunction_3d.Rd

Evaluates fun on transformed x/y/z scale ranges and passes the scalar field to the same extraction used by stat_isosurface_3d. Since fun is known everywhere, each vertex on a grid edge is then moved onto fun = level by refine Illinois regula falsi steps inside the edge whose endpoints bracket the level, and vertex normals (nx, ny, nz) are central differences of fun at the final vertices, with steps of 1e-5 times each axis range. Vertices that lie on no grid edge (merged "tetra" clusters, centre vertices of "cubes") keep their position and take the normal from fun.

Usage

stat_isofunction_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomStatsSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  fun,
  n = 24L,
  args = list(),
  levels = NULL,
  caps = FALSE,
  method = NULL,
  refine = 2L,
  adaptive = FALSE,
  depth = c(4L, 8L),
  tol = 0.002,
  simplify = NULL,
  clip = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE,
  render = c("mesh", "trace"),
  trace_tolerance = 1e-05,
  trace_steps = 512L
)

geom_isofunction_3d(...)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

geom

Geom prototype for keyed triangle corners.

fun

Vectorised scalar function of x, y and z, or a signed distance function (sdf_sphere()).

n

Grid resolution, scalar or three integers.

args

Additional named arguments passed to fun.

levels

Numeric scalar-field thresholds; NULL uses pretty levels.

caps

Whether to cap the sublevel region on the box faces (and on the clipping plane).

method

Extraction method: "cubes" (the default on a grid), "tetra", "dual" (the default with adaptive = TRUE) or "nets".

refine

Number of regula falsi steps per edge vertex; 0 keeps the linear interpolation of the gridded values.

adaptive

Whether to extract on an octree refined by interval arithmetic instead of a grid.

depth

Minimum and maximum octree depth; depth d splits each axis into 2^d intervals.

tol

Geometric tolerance of the octree, relative to the diagonal of the scale box.

simplify

NULL, or a target face count (or fraction of the extracted faces) to which the surface is reduced by quadric edge collapse (mesh_decimate()). Normals are then recomputed from the decimated faces, or from fun in stat_isofunction_3d().

clip

NULL, or a plane made with sdf_plane(). The surface keeps the part on the side the plane normal points away from. With caps = TRUE the sublevel region is also closed on the plane, as with MATLAB's isocaps: each grid cell is split into the six tetrahedra of method = "tetra", the plane cuts each in a triangle or quad on which the linear interpolant of the field is linear, and the part of that polygon below the level is filled, as on the box faces. Plane caps point along the plane normal. The plane is in transformed position coordinates.

render

"mesh" extracts triangles. "trace" sphere-traces an SDF with an opaque fill per raster sample. In the raster backend the traced surface composites at its depth with the other layers, translucent ones included; vector and hybrid panels place it as an image, and vector primitives behind it are hidden. Intrinsic primitives require backend_3d("raymarch"). Tracing uses transformed scale coordinates inside the panel box; these are geometry chart coordinates for the intrinsic backend.

trace_tolerance

Surface tolerance in transformed scale units.

trace_steps

Maximum sphere-tracing steps per ray.

Details

adaptive = TRUE replaces the grid by an octree over the scale box (Plantinga and Vegter 2004). fun is evaluated on whole boxes in interval arithmetic, which encloses its range and gradient over each box. A box whose range contains no level is dropped. Every other box is split down to depth[1], and further, up to depth[2], while the inner product of its gradient enclosure with itself may reach zero (the small normal variation test: without it the level set inside the box can fold) or while the box diagonal times r / |c| exceeds tol times the diagonal of the scale box, where c and r are the centre and half diagonal of the gradient enclosure. Every gradient in the box then lies within asin(r / |c|) of c, so tol bounds how far the level set bends away from a plane inside a box. Gradients are measured with each axis scaled to the unit interval. The surface is then extracted by dual contouring on the octree (Ju et al. 2002): each sign change on a minimal edge, an edge no smaller box subdivides, gives one polygon through the vertices of the three or four boxes around it, so boxes of different sizes join without cracks. Each box carries one vertex per level-curve loop on its faces, as with method = "dual" on a grid. Edge crossings are placed by refine regula falsi steps and their normals come from fun. Only method = "dual" (the default with adaptive = TRUE) and "nets" apply; n is not used.

fun is evaluated on interval objects, so it may use +, -, *, /, ^, abs(), sqrt(), exp(), expm1(), log(), log1p(), log2(), log10(), sin(), cos(), sinh(), cosh(), tanh(), atan(), min(), max(), and pmin() and pmax() called in its own body. Any other operation, including comparisons and ifelse(), stops with an error that names the call.

fun may be a signed distance function built with sdf_sphere() and sdf_blend(). levels then defaults to 0, and vertex normals (with the crossing normals of "dual") come from the exact gradient of its expression tree in place of central differences.

References

Dowell and Jarratt (1971). A modified regula falsi method for computing the root of an equation. BIT 11, 168-174. doi:10.1007/BF01934364

Plantinga and Vegter (2004). Isotopic approximation of implicit curves and surfaces. Symposium on Geometry Processing, 251-260. https://diglib.eg.org/handle/10.2312/SGP.SGP04.251-260

Ju, Losasso, Schaefer and Warren (2002). Dual contouring of Hermite data. ACM Transactions on Graphics 21, 339-346. doi:10.1145/566654.566586

Examples

ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_isofunction_3d(fun = function(x, y, z) x^2 + y^2 + z^2,
                     n = 10, levels = 0.5) + coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  stat_isofunction_3d(fun = function(x, y, z) x^2 + y^2 + z^2,
                     n = 8, levels = 0.5) + coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_isofunction_3d(fun = function(x, y, z) x^2 + y^2 + z^2,
                     levels = 0.5, adaptive = TRUE, depth = c(2, 4)) +
  coord_3d()
